questions.explain: A read replica's TCO has four components: compute (instance hourly rate), storage (SQL Server replicas each carry a full data copy — a 5TB primary with two replicas bills 15TB), data transfer (same-AZ free; cross-AZ $0.01/GB; cross-region $0.02–$0.09/GB — 500GB/day cross-region = $300–$1,350/mo in transfer alone), and I/O (gp3 provisioned IOPS per instance).
options: Only the compute hourly rate
Compute and storage only
Compute, storage (full copy per replica), data transfer (cross-AZ $0.01/GB, cross-region $0.02–$0.09/GB), and I/O — e.g., one idle db.r6i.2xlarge readable standby ≈ $1,898/mo
Replicas are free with the primary

questions.explain: The weekly audit pulls 7-day averages of ReadIOPS, DatabaseConnections, CPUUtilization, and ReplicaLag for every replica: flag IDLE_CANDIDATE_FOR_DELETION when avg ReadIOPS < 10 and connections < 5; flag UNDERUTILIZED_CONSIDER_DOWNSIZING when CPU < 10% and ReadIOPS < 50. The most common waste pattern is the replica nobody reads — reporting moved to a warehouse or the connection string was never updated.
options: Flag IDLE_CANDIDATE_FOR_DELETION when ReadIOPS < 10 and connections < 5; UNDERUTILIZED_CONSIDER_DOWNSIZING when CPU < 10% and ReadIOPS < 50

questions.explain: Core equation: cost of replica < cost of primary upgrade needed to handle the same read load — e.g., db.r6i.2xlarge primary at 85% CPU from analytics: upgrading to 4xlarge adds $1,898/mo vs a db.r6i.xlarge replica at $949/mo, saving $11,388/year; a 1-year RI on the 2xlarge is ~$1,196/mo (37% off). Recommendation logic: CPU ≥ 70% with read fraction ≥ 50% and savings ≥ 0 → ADD_READ_REPLICA; write-bound → UPGRADE_PRIMARY_WRITE_BOUND.
options: Always add replicas; never upgrade the primary

Cost of replica < cost of primary upgrade for the same read load — e.g., a smaller replica ($949/mo) vs primary upgrade (+$1,898/mo) saves $11,388/yr; add a replica when CPU ≥ 70% and the load is read-dominated
Replicas always save money
The break-even is always exactly one year

questions.explain: Unlike engines with shared-storage clusters, SQL Server replicas each carry a full copy: 5TB primary + 2 replicas = 15TB of gp3 at $0.115/GB-month = $1,725/month just in storage. Cross-region replication at 500GB/day of log traffic costs $300–$1,350/month in transfer before a single query runs.
options: Replica storage is free
Storage is shared so replicas add no storage cost
Only compute matters cross-region

On the replica itself, check sys.dm_exec_query_stats for actual query load and connection counts — a replica serving a dozen queries an hour is not earning its keep.
